name: Similar pages agent
job: Finds pages like ours and like the ones we studied, in India and abroad, for the scout to look at.
step: Done: 39 pages (38 sure, 1 unsure), 13 findings, 11 ideas. All second-hand until the scout looks.
did: Searched public rankings, agency lists, press articles and tool-seller case studies (no Instagram opened).
Listed 39 pages: 38 with the handle shown by at least one source, 1 unsure.
Wrote 13 findings on prices, buyers, formats and auto-DM rules; seller numbers are marked as claims.
Wrote 11 content ideas, each tied to a page or source.

findings.title: Small Hindi pages can get reels far bigger than their follower count
findings.detail: A creator-tracking site lists a 47K Hindi astrology/numerology page (astro_anubhhvmishra) with top reels of 6.4M, 4.7M and 4.5M, and a 219K numerology page (ankitbatraofficial) with 0.9M to 1.5M. The site does not label the metric (probably views). Not seen by us yet.

findings.title: The biggest page in the field mixes astrology with mythology stories and animation
findings.detail: Astro Arun Pandit (about 2.4M followers) is listed with topics including mythological stories and Ramayana animation next to zodiac and remedies; listed top reels 2.9M to 4M. Suggests story + animation is used to reach people, astrology to sell. Second-hand.

findings.title: Typical paid reading prices in India: Rs 150 to 700 a session
findings.detail: A May 2025 explainer puts usual online session prices at Rs 150 to 700, with Astrotalk ranging from Rs 99 quick chats to Rs 1,999 long video sessions. A paid PDF report sits naturally inside or below this band.

findings.title: Most money comes from people who already bought once
findings.detail: Astrotalk's founder is quoted saying over 82% of monthly revenue comes from existing customers; consultations were about 91% of FY26 revenue (Rs 1,657 crore of Rs 1,823 crore). For us: a second and third report for past buyers matters as much as new buyers.

findings.title: Who buys: mostly women aged 25 to 35, relationship and marriage questions first
findings.detail: An Astroyogi survey cited in 2025 says most users were 25 to 35 and 60% female, with relationships the top Gen Z topic; Astrotalk's founder names marriage concerns as the most common reason to consult.

findings.title: What Indian tarot pages sell: consultations first, then products and courses
findings.detail: Across two Indian lists, pages sell personal consultations and structured readings, spiritual product shops, booking websites and tarot courses. Almost none is described as selling a low-priced PDF report through a reel series, which may be an open gap for us. No prices were published.

findings.title: Formats named again and again for tarot pages
findings.detail: Lists describe the same handful: free and yes/no readings, pick-a-card posts, monthly zodiac + tarot readings, remedies and tips, client stories/testimonials, and tarot-learning explainers.

findings.title: CLAIM (vendor): one 'comment for the link' reel brought 28,610 followers
findings.detail: SuperProfile's own case study says creator technovert.yogi got 28,610 new followers, 30,217 automatic replies and 31,742 link clicks from one reel. It is the tool seller's marketing, a tech topic, and unverified.

findings.title: Auto-DM rules that shape the keyword
findings.detail: SuperProfile's guide says: one private reply per comment, only within 7 days of the comment; follow-ups only if the person replies, within 24 hours; the exact full word must be typed unless paid intent matching is on (it says that catches Hinglish and misspellings). So: one short, easy-to-spell keyword.

findings.title: CLAIM (vendor): DM open and conversion rates
findings.detail: ManyChat's blog claims DMs get 70 to 90% opens in the first hours and qualified DM leads convert at 12 to 20%; it also suggests adding typo versions of the keyword. Seller's numbers, no independent check.

findings.title: Engagement rate is not tied to size
findings.detail: In one agency list, a 22.6K healing/numerology page shows 16.14% engagement and a 192.7K tarot page 9.65%, while a 98.2K page shows 2.27%. Agency-measured, method not given; the scout should look at what the high ones post.

findings.title: Astrology brands treat Instagram as the place for short, shareable pieces
findings.detail: A trade article says astro apps use Instagram for short reels, testimonials, polls and Q&As, and long explainers on YouTube; Astroyogi describes a 'curious explorer' group that comes for memes and daily horoscopes before the serious buyers.

findings.title: Long AI-made mythology series are being built for Instagram
findings.detail: Collective Artists Network's Historyverse Mahabharata is reported as 600+ AI-made episodes of 3 to 4 minutes aimed at Instagram; and the 'Mahabharat with Divyansh' page is reported to have gained 100,000 followers in 11 days with one-minute narrated reels. Handles were not printed, so neither is in the page list.

ideas.title: Mulank ki kahani, cartoon mein
ideas.hook: Mulank 1 se 9 tak, har number ka ek chhota sa cartoon kirdaar. Aaj milte hain Mulank 3 se.
ideas.format: 9-episode motion-graphic series, one drawn character per mulank, same opening every time
ideas.borrowed_from: astroarunpandit (story + animation mix) and sanctuarywrld (drawn sign characters)
ideas.why: Both pages are only described by third-party sites; we have not seen how their animation looks. Fits our motion-graphic skill, so cheap to test.

ideas.title: Ek topic, nau mulank
ideas.hook: Shaadi ki shopping pe har mulank kya karta hai? Apna number dhoondo.
ideas.format: One everyday situation, nine quick cards (one per mulank), text-led motion graphic
ideas.why: Described in a magazine list as a repeatable text format; people tend to send 'their number' to friends, but that is our guess until the scout checks numbers.

ideas.title: Mulank ka pie chart
ideas.hook: Mulank 5 ka dimaag kis cheez mein kitna lagta hai? Yeh raha chart.
ideas.format: Animated pie chart or Venn diagram per mulank, 10 to 15 seconds, save-able last frame
ideas.borrowed_from: lookupthestarsastro (charts and Venn diagrams of sign traits)
ideas.why: Second-hand description only. Easy for us to render as true motion graphics.

ideas.title: Mulank bingo
ideas.hook: Mulank 7 wale, isme se kitne box tick hote hain? Comment mein number likho.
ideas.format: Bingo card that fills box by box; viewer counts their ticks
ideas.why: The format is named in a magazine list; no numbers seen. Counting along gives a reason to comment without any promise.

ideas.title: Do mulank, ek rishta
ideas.hook: Mulank 2 aur Mulank 8 saath mein kaise chalte hain? Aaj inki jodi dekhte hain.
ideas.format: Compatibility pair series, two characters on screen, ends with keyword for the paid compatibility report
ideas.borrowed_from: ankitbatraofficial (birth-number relationship advice) and sarahmoodyofficial (compatibility guides leading to readings)
ideas.why: Relationship questions are reported as the top reason people pay for readings; the page formats themselves are second-hand until the scout looks.

ideas.title: Aaj ka chhota sa kaam
ideas.hook: Aaj bas ek kaam: apni janm tareekh likho aur dekho aapka personal year number kya banta hai.
ideas.format: Do-this-task reel: viewer calculates along on screen, then keyword for the full personal-year report
ideas.borrowed_from: tarotbysakshirajput (manifestation techniques, per a Delhi list) plus our study of pagetkagy
ideas.why: The Indian page is only listed in an article; the task format was seen on pagetkagy. Calculation is real and checkable, no result is promised.

ideas.title: Card chuno: 1, 2 ya 3
ideas.hook: Teen card saamne hain. Jo pehle achha lage woh chuno, phir apna message suno.
ideas.format: Pick-a-card reel with animated card flip; three short messages; free reading, paid report mentioned softly at the end
ideas.borrowed_from: theguidinglight.byiknoor and nirvaandestiny (pick-a-card and yes/no readings)
ideas.why: Lists name pick-a-card as a standard format for Indian tarot pages; we have no retention numbers for it yet.

ideas.title: Mahine ka tarot, mulank ke hisaab se
ideas.hook: December ka message, Mulank 4 ke liye. Agle mahine phir milenge, isi din.
ideas.format: Monthly reading per mulank posted on a fixed date each month
ideas.why: Monthly readings are described in one list only. A fixed date gives a reason to come back; needs the scout to confirm how others time it.

ideas.title: Akashic reading kya hoti hai, 5 episodes mein
ideas.hook: Akashic reading mein hota kya hai? Paanch chhote episodes mein seedhi baat.
ideas.format: 5-part explainer series in motion graphics, each ends with next episode's question
ideas.borrowed_from: prateekbajaj_akashic_records (largest Indian Akashic page on a ranking site)
ideas.why: We only know the page exists and its size; how it explains Akashic work is unseen. Explaining first should make the paid reading easier to understand.

ideas.title: Tarot mein yeh karo, yeh nahi
ideas.hook: Tarot reading lene se pehle 3 cheezein karo, aur 2 cheezein mat karo.
ideas.borrowed_from: mehraneha_ (tarot explained on video) and the myth-busting format named in a vendor blog
ideas.why: The vendor blog is marketing and the page is only listed; honest, useful advice builds trust before a paid offer.

ideas.title: Ek shabd likho, report DM mein
ideas.hook: Apna mulank report chahiye? Comment mein sirf MULANK likho, link DM mein aa jayega.
ideas.format: Closing card for every series episode: one short keyword, same word all series
ideas.borrowed_from: SuperProfile guide and technovert.yogi case study
ideas.why: The numbers are the tool seller's own claims. The guide's rules (exact word, one reply, 7-day window) are practical and worth following.
